_comment: Chapter 5.2 as facts: which marks and labels a package carries, how large they must be, and when each may be left off. Read verbatim from the official editions with scripts/read_land_regulations.py and transcribed here by hand; only the values belong in this repository, never the text. Every rule names the provision it came from, so a reader can check it against the book. A compilation offered as an aid; the published regulation remains authoritative. Sizes are millimetres. A null minimum means the provision gives no figure, which is a fact in itself and not an omission.

source.adr: ADR 2025 Volume II (ECE/TRANS/352 Vol. II), chapter 5.2, pages 245-252
source.rid: RID 2025 (Appendix C to COTIF, Annex), chapter 5.2, page 828
source.imdg: IMDG Code Amendment 42-24 (IMO resolution MSC.556(108)), chapter 5.2, pages 281-292

_rid_adn_mirror_adr: Checked, not assumed. RID 5.2.2.2.1.1 and ADN 5.2.2.2.1.1 were quoted side by side with the ADR and are identical word for word, down to the figure, the three asterisk notes, the 100 x 100 mm minimum, the 5 mm inner line and the colour rule for its two halves; the battery mark of 5.2.1.9.2 likewise. The rules below therefore carry all three provision numbers. The IMDG Code is the exception and is kept apart, because it numbers this chapter differently.
_imdg_numbering_differs: The IMDG Code does not follow the ADR sub-numbering of chapter 5.2. Its marking provisions for radioactive material sit at 5.2.1.5.x where the ADR has 5.2.1.7.x, so an IMDG rule must never be cited by its ADR number. Only the label provisions of 5.2.2.2 were found to share their numbering, and those are marked as verified where they appear below.

un_number.text: The UN number of the goods contained, preceded by the letters "UN", clearly and durably marked on each package.

character_height_mm.when: packages of 30 l capacity or less, or 30 kg maximum net mass or less, and cylinders of 60 l water capacity or less
packages of 5 l capacity or less, or 5 kg maximum net mass or less

un_number.unpackaged_articles: The mark is displayed on the article, on its cradle, or on its handling, storage or launching device.

proper_shipping_name.text: For goods of Class 1 the package additionally bears the proper shipping name determined under 3.1.2, clearly legible and indelible, in one or more languages of which one shall be French, German or English unless the countries concerned have agreed otherwise.

also_required_for_radioactive.text: For each package other than an excepted package, the UN number preceded by "UN" and the proper shipping name, legibly and durably marked on the outside.

salvage.text: Salvage packagings, large salvage packagings and salvage pressure receptacles additionally bear the word "SALVAGE".

environmentally_hazardous.required_when: the substance meets the criteria of 2.2.9.1.10
exempt_when: single packagings, and inner packagings of combination packagings, containing 5 l or less for liquids
single packagings, and inner packagings of combination packagings, containing a net mass of 5 kg or less for solids

placement.text: Adjacent to the marks required by 5.2.1.1; the requirements of 5.2.1.2 and 5.2.1.4 apply.

environmentally_hazardous.symbol: fish and tree, black on white or a suitable contrasting background

reduction.condition: if the size of the package so requires, provided the mark remains clearly visible

environmentally_hazardous.note: The labelling provisions of 5.2.2 apply in addition to this mark.

battery.required_when: packages containing lithium cells or batteries, or sodium ion cells or batteries, prepared in accordance with special provision 188 or 400 of Chapter 3.3
battery.several_un_numbers: Where a package contains cells or batteries assigned to different UN numbers, all applicable UN numbers are indicated on one or more marks.
battery.shape: rectangle or square with hatched edging
battery.symbol: group of batteries, one damaged and emitting flame, above the UN number(s); black on white or a suitable contrasting background

reduction.condition: if the size of the package so requires

figure.why: The printed figure is wrapped in dimension annotations that abut its hatched edging, so a crop box around the whole mark takes the annotations with it. Everything except the symbol is stated in words - a rectangle 100 mm by 100 mm, red hatched edging at least 5 mm wide, the symbol above the UN number(s) - so the frame is built from those values and the symbol is the edition's own.
figure.asterisk: The figure prints an asterisk where the UN number goes. An asterisk is a footnote in a book; on a package it says nothing, so the sheet prints the number of the cells actually inside.

required_for: combination packagings having inner packagings containing liquids
closed or open cryogenic receptacles intended for the carriage of refrigerated liquefied gases
machinery or apparatus containing liquid dangerous goods when it is required to ensure the liquid remains in its intended orientation (special provision 301)
exempt: outer packagings containing pressure receptacles, except closed or open cryogenic receptacles

outer packagings containing dangerous goods in inner packagings each containing not more than 120 ml, with sufficient absorbent material between inner and outer packagings to completely absorb the liquid contents
outer packagings containing Class 6.2 infectious substances in primary receptacles each containing not more than 50 ml
Type IP-2, Type IP-3, Type A, Type B(U), Type B(M) or Type C packages containing Class 7 radioactive material
outer packagings containing articles which are leak-tight in all orientations, such as alcohol or mercury in thermometers, or aerosols
outer packagings containing dangerous goods in hermetically sealed inner packagings each containing not more than 500 ml
orientation_arrows.placement: On two opposite vertical sides of the package, arrows pointing in the correct upright direction.
orientation_arrows.appearance: Two black or red arrows on white or a suitable contrasting background, rectangular; the rectangular border is optional. Either the figure of 5.2.1.10.1 or arrows meeting ISO 780:1997.

size.requirement: of a size clearly visible commensurate with the size of the package
size._no_prescribed_size: 5.2.1.10.1 gives no dimension at all: the arrows must be 'of a size that is clearly visible commensurate with the size of the package', which is a judgement about the package. Any size a sheet prints them at is that sheet's choice and must be named as one.

prohibition.text: Arrows for purposes other than indicating proper package orientation shall not be displayed on a package marked under this sub-section.

figures.5.2.1.10.1.1: the arrows without a rectangular border (printed on the left)
figures.5.2.1.10.1.2: the same arrows inside a rectangular border (printed on the right)
figures._how_told_apart: The two figures are identical apart from the border, and the print sets both captions on one line, so they were matched to the drawings by the captions' own x position measured off the page.

requirements: able to withstand open weather exposure without a substantial reduction in effectiveness

large_receptacles.text: Intermediate bulk containers of more than 450 litres capacity and large packagings are marked on two opposite sides.

which.text: For each article or substance listed in Table A of Chapter 3.2, the labels shown in Column (5) are affixed unless a special provision in Column (6) provides otherwise.

shape.form: square set at an angle of 45 degrees (diamond)

_which_distance.why: The land and sea provisions say only that a label is a square set at 45 degrees whose minimum dimensions are 100 mm x 100 mm, which leaves two readings: the square's side, or the diamond's bounding box. The two differ by the square root of two, and printing the wrong one makes every label the wrong size while looking right. Measuring the figures in the official editions did not settle it — the ADR draws the 5 mm inner line at a spacing of 0.51 pt on a 96.89 pt side, which is the stroke width of the outline rather than the inner line, so the drawing is schematic on this point. What settles it is the same label written out in full elsewhere: 49 CFR 172.407(c)(1) prescribes the identical shape, the identical 100 mm and the identical 5 mm border measured from the outside edge, and says 'at least 100 mm (3.9 inches) on each side'. The side is therefore the 100 mm, and a full-size label is about 141.4 mm from point to point.
sources: UN Recommendations on the Transport of Dangerous Goods, Model Regulations — https://unece.org/transport/dangerous-goods/un-model-regulations-rev-24
_which_distance.consequence: One full-size label to an A4 sheet. Two side by side need 283 mm across a 210 mm page, which is impossible; two stacked need 283 mm of a 297 mm page, which leaves 14 mm for margins, caption and cut marks together.

shape.inner_line_colour: Upper half the same colour as the symbol; lower half the same colour as the class or division number in the bottom corner.

reduction.condition: proportionally, if the size of the package so requires, provided the symbols and other elements remain clearly visible

layout.bottom_corner: The class, or for Classes 4.1, 4.2 and 4.3 the figure "4", or for Classes 6.1 and 6.2 the figure "6".
layout.top_half: The class symbol, or for divisions 1.4, 1.5 and 1.6 the division number, or for model No. 7E the word "FISSILE".
layout.bottom_half: Additional text, numbers, symbols or letters, mandatory where the model requires them and optional otherwise.

boundary.text: Labels are displayed on a background of contrasting colour, or have either a dotted or a solid outer boundary line.

rules: affixed to the same surface of the package, if the dimensions of the package allow; for packages of Class 1 and Class 7, near the mark indicating the proper shipping name
so placed that the label is not covered or obscured by any part or attachment to the packaging, or by any other label or mark
displayed next to each other when more than one label is required
placement.irregular_packages: Where a package is of such an irregular shape or small size that a label cannot be satisfactorily affixed, the label may be attached by a securely affixed tag or other suitable means.

two_opposite_sides.text: Intermediate bulk containers of more than 450 litres capacity and large packagings are labelled on two opposite sides.

cylinders.text: Cylinders for Class 2 may bear labels, and the environmentally hazardous substance mark where appropriate, reduced according to ISO 7225:2005 for display on the non-cylindrical part (shoulder). Labels may overlap to the extent ISO 7225:2005 provides for, but the primary hazard label and the figures on any label remain fully visible and the symbols recognizable. Where the diameter is too small, the reduced labels may be displayed on the cylindrical part.

rules: The label conforming to model No. 4.1 implies the product may be flammable, so no label conforming to model No. 3 is required.

For self-reactive substances of Type B a label conforming to model No. 1 is applied as well, unless the competent authority has permitted it to be dispensed with for a specific packaging on test data.
The label conforming to model No. 5.2 implies the product may be flammable, so no label conforming to model No. 3 is required.
For organic peroxides of Type B a label conforming to model No. 1 is applied as well, on the same condition.
A label conforming to model No. 8 is required for organic peroxides when the Packing Group I or II criteria of Class 8 are met.
self_reactive_and_organic_peroxides.named_substances: For self-reactive substances and organic peroxides mentioned by name, the labels to be affixed are listed in 2.2.41.4 and 2.2.52.4 respectively.

infectious_substances.text: In addition to the label conforming to model No. 6.2, packages of infectious substances bear any other label required by the nature of the contents.

radioactive_material.text: Each package, overpack and container bears the labels conforming to models Nos. 7A, 7B or 7C according to the category, affixed to two opposite sides. Packages containing fissile material other than that excepted under 2.2.7.2.3.5 bear labels conforming to model No. 7E in addition.

imdg._comment: The sea regime in its own right, not as a delta on the road one. Recorded separately because the IMDG Code numbers this chapter differently and, on two points that reach the sheet, requires something the land regulations do not.

provision_map._comment: Which IMDG provision answers the question each ADR provision answers. Anything not listed here has not been read.
provision_map.5.2.1.1: 5.2.1.1 (marking), and the proper shipping name too — see proper_shipping_name below

proper_shipping_name.difference: The IMDG Code requires the proper shipping name on EVERY package, alongside the UN number. The land regulations require it only for Class 1 (5.2.1.5) and for radioactive material (5.2.1.7.2). A sea consignment therefore carries a mark a road consignment does not.
proper_shipping_name.text: The proper shipping name determined in accordance with 3.1.2 and the corresponding UN number, preceded by the letters "UN", shall be displayed on each package.
proper_shipping_name.example_given_in_the_code: CORROSIVE LIQUID, ACIDIC, ORGANIC, N.O.S. (caprylyl chloride) UN 3265

un_number_character_height_mm.when: packages of 30 L capacity or less, or 30 kg maximum net mass or less, and cylinders of 60 L water capacity or less
packages of 5 L capacity or less, or 5 kg maximum net mass or less

division_1_4_s.text: For goods of division 1.4, compatibility group S, the division and compatibility group letter shall also be marked, unless the label for 1.4S is displayed.

requirements: such that the information will still be identifiable on packages surviving at least three months' immersion in the sea; in considering suitable marking methods, account shall be taken of the durability of the packaging materials used and the surface of the package
displayed on a background of contrasting colour on the external surface of the package
not located with other package marks that could substantially reduce their effectiveness
durability.difference: The three months' immersion requirement has no counterpart in ADR, RID or ADN, whose 5.2.1.2 asks only that a mark withstand open weather exposure. It is the reason a sheet printed on office paper can never be presented as sufficient for a sea consignment.

marine_pollutant.name: marine pollutant mark, not the environmentally hazardous substance mark
marine_pollutant.required_when: packages containing marine pollutants meeting the criteria of 2.9.3, except as provided in 2.10.2.7
exempt_when: the substance also meets the criteria for inclusion in a hazard class from 1 to 9, except class 7, AND is packaged in single or combination packagings containing a net quantity per single or inner packaging of 5 l or less for liquids, or a net mass per single or inner packaging of 5 kg or less for solids
marine_pollutant.placement: Adjacent to the marks required by 5.2.1.1; the provisions of 5.2.1.2 and 5.2.1.4 shall be met.
marine_pollutant.symbol: fish and tree, black on white or a suitable contrasting background

reduction.condition: if the size of the package so requires, provided the mark remains clearly visible

marine_pollutant.note: The labelling provisions of 5.2.2 apply in addition to the marine pollutant mark.

exemption.text: Marine pollutants also meeting the criteria for inclusion in a hazard class from 1 to 9 (except class 7), and packaged in single or combination packagings containing a net quantity per single or inner packaging of 5 l or less for liquids or having a net mass per single or inner packaging of 5 kg or less for solids, are not subject to 5.2.1.6, 5.3.2.3, 5.4.1.4.3.6 and 7.1.4.2. These provisions do not apply to substances transported under UN 3077 or UN 3082 (see special provision 375).
exemption.difference_from_land: The threshold is the same 5 l and 5 kg the land regulations use, but it is fenced twice over. It reaches only substances that also fall in a hazard class from 1 to 9 other than 7, and it is expressly withheld from UN 3077 and UN 3082 — the two generic environmentally hazardous entries, which are exactly the ones a reader would expect it to cover. Those two therefore always carry the mark, whatever the packaging holds.
also_relieves: 5.3.2.3 (the mark on the cargo transport unit)

orientation_arrows.note: The four cases requiring arrows and the exemptions read identically to ADR 5.2.1.10, allowing for the Code's own list numbering and its use of mL and L.

which_labels.difference: The land regulations name the labels in one place: column (5) of Table A. The IMDG Code takes the primary label from the class in column 3 of the Dangerous Goods List and every subsidiary label from column 4, with column 6 able to add one where column 4 shows none, or remove one where it does.
text: Labels identifying primary and subsidiary hazards conform to models Nos. 1 to 9 illustrated in 5.2.2.2.2. The "EXPLOSIVE" subsidiary hazard label is model No. 1.

Where articles or substances are specifically listed in the Dangerous Goods List, a danger class label is affixed for the hazard shown in column 3. A subsidiary hazard label is also affixed for any hazard indicated by a class or division number in column 4. Special provisions in column 6 may require a subsidiary hazard label where none is indicated in column 4, or may exempt one that is.

low_degree_of_danger.text: A package containing a dangerous substance of a low degree of danger may be exempt from these labelling requirements, in which case a special provision saying so appears in column 6. For certain substances the package is instead marked with the text the special provision gives — baled hay (UN 1327) and fish meal (UN 1374) are the examples the Code prints.

multi_class_not_listed_by_name.text: Where a substance meeting the definition of more than one class is not listed by name in the Dangerous Goods List, chapter 2.0 determines the primary hazard class, and subsidiary labels are applied as the List specifies.

other_symbols_allowed.text: These provisions relate essentially to danger labels. Additional marks or symbols indicating precautions for handling or storage — an umbrella meaning keep dry, for instance — may be displayed on a package if appropriate.

label_halves.text: Except for labels of divisions 1.4, 1.5 and 1.6, the upper half of the label contains the pictorial symbol and the lower half contains the class number 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.1, 5.2, 6, 7, 8 or 9 as appropriate. For label model No. 9A the upper half contains only the seven vertical stripes of the symbol and the lower half contains the group of batteries and the class number. Except for model No. 9A the label may include text such as the UN number or words describing the hazard class, provided the text does not obscure or detract from the other required elements.

battery.name: lithium battery mark
battery.difference: ADR, RID and ADN place this mark at 5.2.1.9. The IMDG Code has it at 5.2.1.10, which is where the land regulations put the orientation arrows — the clearest example of why an IMDG rule must never be cited by an ADR number.
battery.found_via: Special provision 188, which cross-refers to 'the mark as shown in 5.2.1.10 (lithium battery mark)', and a transitional note allowing the Amendment 40-20 version of that mark, showing a telephone number, to be applied until 31 December 2026.

special_provision_188.label_named: Model No. 9A of 5.2.2.2.2 is named in the provision alongside the mark.
exempt_when: packages containing only button cell batteries installed in equipment, including circuit boards
packages containing no more than four cells or two batteries installed in equipment, where there are not more than two packages in the consignment
special_provision_188.overpack: Where packages are placed in an overpack, the lithium or sodium battery mark is either clearly visible or reproduced on the outside, and the overpack is marked "OVERPACK" in lettering at least 12 mm high.
other_conditions: each package withstands a 1.2 m drop test in any orientation, except where cells or batteries are installed in equipment
packages do not exceed 30 kg gross mass, except where cells or batteries are installed in or packed with equipment

label_durability.text: The method of affixing the labels, or applying stencils of labels, is such that they will still be identifiable on packages surviving at least three months' immersion in the sea. Account is taken of the durability of the packaging materials used and the surface of the package.
label_durability.note: 5.2.1.2 says the same for marks. The Code therefore asks it twice, once for marks and once for labels, which is why the sheet's note names both.

class_9_label_model.answer: 9A on the package, 9 on the unit
class_9_label_model.why: The Dangerous Goods List's column 3 gives the class, not the label model, so it says plain 9 for the lithium and sodium battery entries and cannot by itself choose between models 9 and 9A. Three provisions settle it together. 5.2.2.2.1.3 gives model 9A a layout of its own — the seven stripes alone in the upper half, the batteries and the class number in the lower. Special provision 188 names model No. 9A beside the lithium battery mark. And 5.3.1.1.2 says that for class 9 the placard corresponds to model No. 9 and that model No. 9A shall not be used for placarding purposes, which is a prohibition that only means anything if 9A is a package label. So the Code separates the two on the package/unit axis, and Table A column (5) already names 9A per entry for the same substances.
class_9_label_model.consequence: For the sea regime the package label follows Table A column (5) where that gives 9A, and the class from column 3 otherwise. The placarding check was already right to refuse 9A on a unit since v1.150.0.

_material_standard.what_it_is: The British Standard for printed pressure-sensitive adhesive-coated labels for marine use. It is the de facto standard by which the labelling trade demonstrates compliance with the IMDG Code's three months' immersion requirement, testing artificial weathering, temperature cycling and an actual three-month seawater immersion for adhesion and colour fastness.
_material_standard.why_recorded: The sheet can say what a compliant label is made of rather than only that paper is not it. Naming the standard is more use to a packer than a warning with no way out.

column_6._comment: What column 6 of the IMDG Dangerous Goods List does to the labels on a package. 5.2.2.1.2 lets a special provision add a subsidiary label where column 4 shows none and remove one where it does; 5.2.2.1.2.1 lets one drop the labelling altogether. Read by scripts/read_imdg_special_provisions.py, which splits chapter 3.3 by the measured position of its provision numbers and found all 262 numbers the column cites. Forty-two of them mention a label, a mark or an exemption; the effects below are what those forty-two say, judged one by one. The rest are listed under 'read_no_effect' so the record shows they were read and not skipped.

29.instead: the package, bale included, is marked with the appropriate class
29.note: Exempt from labelling outright, not on a condition this application cannot see.

63.condition: the aerosol's contents other than the propellant meet class 6.1 or class 8, packing group II or III

133.condition: a packaging other than packing instruction P409 was authorised, and the competent authority of the country of origin has not dispensed with the label

172.condition: one subsidiary hazard label for each subsidiary hazard the radioactive material exhibits; which ones follow from the material, not from this provision

181.condition: unless the competent authority of the country of origin has permitted the label to be dispensed with for the packaging employed

204.condition: model 8 if the smoke-producing substance is corrosive by the class 8 criteria, model 6.1 if it is toxic by inhalation by the class 6.1 criteria

271.condition: the mixture contains not less than 90% phlegmatizer by mass

295.condition: batteries need not be individually marked and labelled if the pallet bears the mark and the label

369.condition: uranium hexafluoride in an excepted package is class 6.1 with radioactivity and corrosivity subsidiary hazards

384.note: The provision that settles 9 against 9A per substance, in as many words: the label is model No. 9A, and only the placard on the cargo transport unit is model No. 9.

397.condition: the mixture holds not less than 19.5% and not more than 23.5% oxygen by volume and no other oxidizing gas

405.condition: the vehicle is not fully enclosed by packagings, crates or other means preventing ready identification

955.condition: the viscous substance and its packaging meet 2.3.2.5

219.condition: packed and marked in accordance with packing instruction P904, and not meeting the class 6.1 or 6.2 criteria

294.condition: safety and wax matches in an outer packaging of at most 25 kg net, packed per packing instruction P407; marking still applies

319.condition: packed and marked in accordance with packing instruction P650

973.condition: exempt from class marking when loaded in a cargo transport unit holding one UN number; the proper shipping name and UN number stay on every package except a bale

column_6._read_no_effect_why: These forty-two were all read. The twenty-four listed here name a mark, an exemption or a subsidiary hazard while doing something other than changing which labels go on the package: classification rules, the watt-hour marking of a battery, the technical name that supplements the proper shipping name, conditions for carriage. Recording them by number is what makes the difference between a provision that was judged and one that was never opened.
